The Overture landed at 26db4df99 with all five phases green -- the first five-phase merge since decision 0426 restored heavy. Its post-heavy artifact commit moved book/src/laboratory/generated/the-history/, and NONE of that movement is attributable to the campaign that carried it. WHAT MOVED: migration events 9 to 11; mean pairwise region overlap 0.0134 to 0.0195; occupied sites 264 to 454 with re-occupied 146 to 279; depth/capacity correlation -0.2017 to -0.1776. WHY IT IS NOT THE OVERTURE. The heavy tier AUTHORS that artifact (one test, history_gates_full_world_and_cross_seed). Decision 0148 took heavy off the merge phase list; 0426 put it back on 2026-08-28. In between, the artifact was last authored on 2026-08-18 -- ELEVEN DAYS, during which every landing that moved world values left it stale with nothing to notice. The first merge after restoration absorbs the entire backlog. PROOF THAT AT LEAST ONE OTHER CAMPAIGN IS IN THERE, rather than an inference: the regenerated prose says migrated to empty VERTICES where the committed version said CELLS. That rename is the-lexicon-of-place, merged ea436c227 on 2026-08-24, five days before this merge, and it appears nowhere in The Overture diff -- whose only non-client, non-docs files are windows/worldgen/src/lib.rs (one additive fn plus an Option observer threaded through build_to) and its test file. An additive callback does not move occupied sites by 190. THE THING TO CARRY: a git blame, a bisect, or a reader asking when did stratigraphy-emerged move will land on merge(the-overture) and be wrong. This is not a defect in 0426 -- restoring the tier is what MADE the artifact current again -- it is the one-time cost of the restoration, paid entirely by whichever campaign merged first, and it is invisible in that campaigns own diff review because the chamber authors the commit after every phase the campaign ran. GENERALISES BEYOND heavy: any authoring path removed from an automatic trigger accrues silent drift, and the artifact looks healthy the whole time because it is committed, tracked and drift-checked against ITSELF. The drift check compares the tree to the tree; it cannot see that the AUTHOR has not run. make rebaseline does not close this gap either -- it explicitly does not run heavy, so a campaign doing everything right locally still cannot observe the backlog it is about to carry.
